title: path_cost OverflowError when finite link_etx * MHRI overflows to inf
description:
python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py: `_require_finite_non_negative_etx` (dfv6/lwo3) rejects NaN/inf *inputs*, but `ParentCandidate.path_cost` still does `round(self.link_etx * min_hop_rank_increase)` with no check on the product.

IEEE 754: 1e307 is finite (math.isinf is False) yet 1e307 * 256 is inf, and Python round(inf) raises OverflowError. A link-metric estimator doing 1.0/max(p, 1e-307) produces this without ever handing inf to process_dio.

Confirmed against current code:
- ParentCandidate(fe80::1, 256, 1e307) constructs (input is finite and non-negative)
- path_cost(256) raises OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
- DodagState.process_dio(..., link_etx=1e307) raises OverflowError, not the documented ValueError

process_dio docstring says it raises ValueError for NaN/inf/negative link_etx. Callers catching only ValueError still crash the DODAG state machine. rust/lichen-rpl path_cost already guards !link_cost.is_finite() on the product and saturates to u16::MAX.

Not a refile of dfv6/lwo3 (input isnan/isinf), xtzn (mhri<=0 at init), or fwne (MaxRankIncrease test now uses independent arithmetic: join cost 512, candidate 256+round(10*256)=2816 > 512+2048).

Fix: in path_cost, if link_etx * mhri is non-finite, return INFINITE_RANK (match Rust). Keep the process_dio ValueError door for true inf/NaN inputs.

Test with an independent oracle (do not call path_cost to compute expected): etx=1e307, mhri=256, product is inf -> expect INFINITE_RANK (or documented ValueError), and a joined node must not change parent/role if the call raises.
close_reason: path_cost saturates a non-finite link_etx*MHRI product to INFINITE_RANK (1e307*256 is inf; no OverflowError). process_dio still ValueError on true NaN/inf inputs. Independent IEEE 754 oracle tests in test_dodag.py. pytest tests/rpl/test_dodag.py tests/rpl/test_dao.py: 96 passed.
